editorial.headline: Senior Living Is Nationally Open, but Not for PMA Registration in Bali
editorial.standfirst: Commercial senior-living accommodation is open to foreign investment nationally, yet Bali’s permanent moratorium blocks its PMA registration today.
editorial.body:
Senior living under this activity means the commercial management of accommodation designed for older residents. It is not simply housing with an older demographic: the accommodation is conceived with supporting facilities, professional caregivers and other professional staff, and with attention to the different activities and limitations an older person may experience. The stated scope also includes senior or elderly tourist accommodation, placing the activity within a broad accommodation-management setting shaped around later-life needs.

The activity is open across the full stated business spectrum: micro, small, medium and large enterprises. That matters because the description is operational rather than merely property-based. Its centre of gravity is the management of a commercially run living environment, supported by people with professional caregiving roles and by facilities calibrated to residents’ needs. Whether the operation is organised at a smaller or larger business scale, the record frames the same essential undertaking: managed accommodation for older people, delivered with professional support.

At the national level, the position is straightforward. The activity is open to PMA, with a maximum foreign ownership ceiling of 100%. In plain terms, foreign investment may hold the full permitted ownership interest nationally. The national opening is grounded in the cited Presidential Regulations, and there is no lower national foreign-ownership cap in this record to qualify that 100% ceiling.

Bali changes the practical answer completely. A foreign investor cannot register this activity in Bali today. At the large-business scale, every stated scope carries a Low or Medium-Low OSS risk classification; Bali’s moratorium, effective from May 2026, blocks PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities across the island on a permanent basis. The national permission is real, but it does not override Bali’s island-wide PMA moratorium. For a senior-living project intended for Bali, the decisive fact is therefore the provincial block, not the national 100% foreign-ownership ceiling.
